The criteria make these concrete: judge.toml:515 says observe each named referrer, :560 prohibits two current grants while preserving both historical grants, :659 checks both competing offers including loser effects, and :704/:713/:722 require exactly one complete ordinary transition per pair with no duplicates. Coordinated lineage (:956) requires exactly one successor for each source; stale-leaf refusal (:1046) checks all members including the valid first member; overlap (:1091) checks one complete winner and no partial loser; receipt/audit/after-images (:1109/:1118/:1127) cover all old/new offers, every member and complete transaction headrooms; reader coverage (:1199) includes every supplied signed-in role. Legitimate side effects are protected: prompt.md:19 explicitly permits generic access/security logs and ordinary extra audit entries without exact global counts. judge.toml:668/:686/:695 restrict stale-refusal invariance to lineage, economic and successful settlement records. :947 permits a draft and access logs on over-budget refusal; :1010 allows the saved preview and logging to grow while economic records stay unchanged. Polish retention checks preserve entered terms rather than demanding immutable whole-page state; corrections/new keys and equivalent date representations are allowed (polish/judge.toml:23/:32/:41/:50).

A conforming implementation that records a denied-access log, adds ordinary audit entries, leaves a failed draft, omits zero financial rows, generates IDs, or omits optional operational seed history is explicitly allowed. These are source-level counterexample assessments, not empirical judge scores.
